what_happened: Dispatch's gap-3 guidance (use manifest.json hooks.context_injection, 'already exercised by the nix and nvim extensions') is structurally unreachable: skill_get_extension_dir() in skill-base.sh resolves the hook by exact task_type equality against the CURRENT dispatched task's own task_type, first-match-wins across loaded extensions -- it never loops/fires across all active extensions. nvim/nix hooks work only because those extensions declare task_type nvim/nix and fire solely on their own domain's tasks. Non-goal (a) forbids sapience from declaring a task_type, and no task will ever carry task_type=sapience, so this hook can never fire for any task of any type. Recommended in report: drop the hook/script deliverable for gap 3 entirely; document session-level-only orientation (ambient SessionStart briefing + on-demand sf1) instead.

Gap-1 fix (permission grants in this repo's extension settings-fragment.json, merging into project-scoped .claude/settings.local.json) is correct for closing the autonomous-dispatch blocker inside this repo, but mcp-server-ownership.md's own rule ('grant permissions at the same scope where the server is registered') says a user-scope-registered server (sapience is registered via ~/.claude.json top-level mcpServers, per nix module activation) should be granted in user-scope ~/.claude/settings.json. The dispatch's chosen project-scope fix is a deliberate, reasoned tradeoff (avoids the dotfiles-enforced-key revert problem) but is repository-scoped, not machine-wide; other projects on this machine will still prompt on the 4 write tools. Documented explicitly in the report's Findings/Risks rather than left implicit.

Plan drops a dispatch-named deliverable (scripts/sapience-context.sh, the gap-3 context_injection hook) after independently re-verifying the research report's refutation: skill_get_extension_dir() in skill-base.sh gates on [ -n "$ext_task_type" ] && [ "$ext_task_type" = "$task_type" ] and returns the first match, so a task_type-less extension's lifecycle hook is unreachable for every task of every type. Non-goal (a) forbids declaring a task_type, so the hook would be dead code. Rationale recorded in plan Non-Goals, Risks, and a dedicated domain note (phase 3).

Two cheap live queries during plan authoring both confirmed the research's carried figures and surfaced a constraint the research missed. jq over ~/.dotfiles/config/claude/settings.json returned exactly the 7 read-only sapience grants, and the same query over .claude/settings.local.json returned 0, re-deriving gap 1 empirically in seconds. Separately, reading .claude/context/index.schema.json surfaced the on_demand:true intent marker requirement (an all-empty-load_when entry WITHOUT it is reported dead by validate-context-budgets.sh) plus the forbidden description/tags/tier keys -- neither appeared in the research report, and both became concrete phase-4 plan items that would otherwise have failed the lint.

Phase 5: README.md's prose naming the dropped gap-3 script literally as 'scripts/sapience-context.sh' tripped check-extension-docs.sh's script-reference check (any .sh filename mentioned in docs but absent from provides.scripts is flagged FAIL) and also violated the plan's own Testing & Validation negative check requiring that exact string to appear nowhere in the extension. Fixed by rephrasing README.md to describe the dropped mechanism without the literal filename.

Phase 5: merging EXTENSION.md into .claude/CLAUDE.md pushed the eager-load total from 67566 B (post phase-1-4 baseline was already drifting slightly) to over the 66800 B gate-20 regression baseline. Resolved by trimming EXTENSION.md from 44 to 28 lines (2253 B to 1407 B), relocating duplicated review-gate-boundary detail to a short pointer, landing eager-load at 66720 B -- 80 B of margin, no baseline move needed. Plan's own 35-45-line target for EXTENSION.md was superseded by this real measured constraint; recorded as a deviation.
